item.title: Swans in fight to keep Matos amid Strasbourg interest
item.description: Vitor Matos spent five years on Jurgen Klopp's staff at Liverpool [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Swansea City look to be facing a fight to hold on to Vitor Matos amid serious interest in their head coach from French top-flight club Strasbourg. Matos is under contract at Swansea until 2030, meaning the Championship side would be due significant compensation should he be lured away. But that has not stopped Strasbourg targeting the 38-year-old Portuguese, who is due to celebrate a year in charge at Swansea later this month. Matos' fellow countryman Hugo Oliveira is the current Strasbourg boss, but is under pressure after a run of five defeats in six matches. Oliveira has managed only three wins in 10 league games since succeeding to Gary O'Neil - who left to become Ipswich Town boss – in July. O'Neil led Strasbourg to an eighth-place finish last season, but they are currently 13th in Ligue 1, only two points above the relegation zone. Strasbourg are a sister club of Premier League side Chelsea. Matos has turned Swansea from potential relegation contenders to promotion hopefuls since taking charge, with the club 20th in the Championship when he took over last November. The Swans finished 11th last season and have made further strides in the first third of this campaign. Vitor Matos led Swansea to seven wins in their first 10 league games of the season, though they have since lost four in five [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Matos' team have been among the early-season pacesetters in the second tier, briefly topping the table, though their form has dipped in recent weeks. Swansea have suffered four defeats in their past five matches, though they remain only three points off top spot going into Saturday's game against West Bromwich Albion. Matos was touted as a contender to take charge at Crystal Palace earlier this season - the Eagles have since appointed Thomas Frank - while he has also been linked with a return to Portugal on the back of his impact with the Swans. In an interview last week, Swansea chief executive Tom Gorringe acknowledged that Matos' impact will not have gone unnoticed at other clubs, though he played down the idea of the former Liverpool coach having his head turned. item.title: Inside Wales' dressing room - how Lake inspired history
item.description: Dewi Lake has captained Wales 24 times [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Inside the Wales dressing room at the Principality Stadium at half-time on Saturday, heads could easily have bowed. Visitors New Zealand had just levelled the scores at 21-21 with the clock in the red at the end of the first half. It was a sucker punch that could have knocked the wind out of Welsh sails. But captain Dewi Lake summoned the words that inspired a first win over New Zealand in 73 years. With a rousing speech, the captain reminded his players of the feeling in the same changing room 12 months earlier, when they trailed by just three points at the break only to eventually lose 52-26. "Dewi made a very good point, the last time that we played them we had been in the contest, but let the dam break," Leicester and Wales wing Gabriel Hamer-Webb told the Rugby Union Weekly podcast. "They slipped through and we promised ourselves that we weren't going to let that happen again, that we had an opportunity to really do something special. "The heart the boys showed from then on, we wanted it more than they did. New Zealand were shocked and there was no way that we were going to let it slip." Gabriel Hamer-Webb won only his second cap in the win over New Zealand [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Hamer-Webb endured a tough time when making his Wales debut in the Six Nations defeat by Scotland in February. He was rewarded for strong club form with a second cap against the All Blacks, coming into the side at the expense of experienced wing Josh Adams. The former Cardiff back is a Test novice, but has already cemented himself as part of Welsh history, with the victory leading to post-match plans being ripped up. Hamer-Webb said: "I had dinner planned with my family for 8.30pm and the boys were telling me that I had to cancel and that there was no way I was going! "The changing room beers after a great win - they are the best moments. "We went into the lounge at the stadium afterwards and there was so much singing and happiness. "We absolutely made the most of it and we understood this was a moment that would go down in history and we had to celebrate properly. "After the game I couldn't walk two metres without somebody congratulating me or someone saying that was one of the best moments of their life," he continued. "My grandfather had never seen us beat the All Blacks, you now start to understand that meant a lot more than us just playing for 80 minutes and getting a win. It meant a lot more." item.title: Scherhant and Wirtz star as Germany reach quarters with beaten Dutch
item.description: Germany's Derry Scherhant celebrates scoring his side's first goal during the UEFA Nations League soccer match between Germany and Netherlands at Olympiastadion Berlin. (is associated with: «Scherhant and Wirtz star as Germany reach quarters with beaten Dutch») Christian Charisius/dpa Derry Scherhant scored his first Germany goal and Florian Wirtz netted twice to send Jürgen Klopp's side into the Nations League quarter-finals after a 5-0 thrashing of the Netherlands, who also go through. The Freiburg winger has been one of the finds of Klopp's early reign and he shone on Monday in the group A2 finale at Berlin's packed Olympic Stadium. Wirtz doubled Germany's lead with an equally stunning strike and Nico Schlotterbeck headed in the third from a free-kick. Wirtz made it 4-0 on 71 minutes and Brajan Gruda capped a strong display with his second international goal. Germany reached March's last eight as group winners ahead of the Dutch, with third-placed Greece empty-handed despite a 1-0 win over bottom side Serbia giving them the same points as the big duo. Scherhant was born in the German capital and it was a homecoming to remember. His grandfather, who used to drive him to youth games in Berlin as a child, was in the stands to watch his breakthrough moment in just his fourth international appearance. Klopp made a slow start to his stewardship after replacing Julian Nagelsmann following another World Cup flop. Germany lost at home to Greece in September, but three handsome wins since put them through. A complicated three-team mini group meant Germany finished top on head-to-heads after winning their 50th meeting with old rivals the Netherlands.

item.title: Wirtz scores twice as Germany thrash Netherlands
item.description: UEFA Nations League Germany 5 - 0 Netherlands FT Florian Wirtz (right) has scored eight goals for Germany since joining Liverpool - only one behind his total for the Reds [Getty Images] Florian Wirtz scored twice as Germany thrashed the Netherlands in their final Nations League game - with both sides qualifying for the quarter-finals. Jurgen Klopp's side started the day third in Group A2 but overtook Greece and the Netherlands into top spot. All three teams ended on 11 points - with results between them being used as the tiebreaker instead of goal difference. Greece, who beat Serbia 1-0 thanks to a Giorgos Masouras goal, finish third. Freiburg's Derry Scherhant scored his first international goal, curling a fine effort into the top corner in Berlin. Liverpool attacking midfielder Wirtz won the ball before firing in Germany's second from outside the box. Borussia Dortmund defender Nico Schlotterbeck headed in Brajan Gruda's free-kick to make it 3-0. Gruda then cut the ball back for Wirtz to lash in his second goal. And Gruda, on loan at Leipzig from Brighton, made it two goals in two caps - to go with his two assists in Berlin - as he made it 5-0. Xavi Hernandez's Netherlands, who beat Greece 7-0 on Friday, finished second.

item.title: Newcastle United Enter Race For 21-Year-Old Defender: Can They Beat Liverpool?
item.description: Newcastle United Enter Race For 21-Year-Old Defender: Can They Beat Liverpool? Newcastle United have entered a crowded race for Lens centre-back Ismaelo Ganiou, according to an exclusive from Pete O’Rourke in Football Insider and its Transfer Insider podcast. The 21-year-old also attracts Liverpool, Chelsea , Manchester City, Tottenham , Paris Saint-Germain, Monaco and Marseille, and nobody leads clearly. Ganiou rejected Crystal Palace, managed by his former Lens coach Pierre Sage, and signed a contract until 2030 in August. A January move looks unlikely because he is recovering from knee surgery until late November. Football Insider expects serious bidding next summer, when Newcastle hope to beat Liverpool by offering a bigger first-team role immediately. What Ganiou brings Ganiou is 6ft 3in, is right-footed, can cover at right-back, and can be compared with Raphael Varane. FotMob ‘s figures from five Ligue 1 starts support the praise: 88% pass accuracy, nine of 14 aerial duels won and 22 clearances in 433 minutes, plus one goal. FotMob values him at roughly £31m. The concerns are availability and physicality. Five starts is a small sample; the knee operation interrupts his season, and Premier League strikers will test his physicality. Why the timing suits Newcastle Jaissle’s front-foot approach needs defenders who recover quickly, yet Newcastle have 12 points from 10 league games and have conceded 16 goals. Dan Burn and Fabian Schar are both 34, and Schar’s contract expires in June 2027. Sven Botman signed until 2030 in January, but he had missed 58 games in his first three and a half years at the club. Can Newcastle United beat Liverpool to this centre-back? COMO, ITALY – AUGUST 01: Gerard Moreno of Villarreal CF is challenged by Ismaelo Ganiou of Racing Club de Lens during the Como Cup 2026 match between RC Lens and Villarreal CF at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on August 01, 2026 in Como, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) They can, provided the starting place is genuine. Liverpool, Chelsea and PSG offer bigger stages, but none can promise a 21-year-old regular football the way Newcastle can with two 34-year-olds in the back line and a defence leaking 1.6 goals a game, including four at both Leeds and Coventry. Schar’s deal ends next summer, so Ganiou would arrive just as a vacancy opens. The doubts are medical and financial. Newcastle spent about £275m on eight signings this summer, including £51m on Matias Fernandez-Pardo, and L’Equipe reported that Lens wanted at least £43m (€50m) when Ganiou renewed. Paying that for a defender coming off knee surgery demands a full medical review and a careful plan for his minutes. If the knee checks out in full, Ganiou solves a problem Jaissle has not yet fixed. A high line needs centre-backs who turn and recover, and neither Burn nor Schar will get quicker.

item.title: McIlroy’s $2 Million Bonus Proves Race To Dubai Still Pays Off
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Rory McIlroy won the 2026 Race to Dubai title on Sunday, securing a record-tying eighth crown and a $2 million bonus check. While the Northern Irishman celebrated the season-long victory, Tyrrell Hatton walked away with more total cash after winning the final tournament. Golf Digest Middle East reported that McIlroy earned an extra $2 million for winning the race, but Hatton’s week in Dubai netted him $3.75 million overall. The money breakdown shows a clear split between the season-long race and the week’s tournament purse. McIlroy finished second in the DP World Tour Championship, taking home $1.26 million for his runner-up spot. Hatton claimed the tournament title with a five-shot victory, collecting $3 million for the win. The Two-Tier Payout System Many fans focus on the Race to Dubai trophy, but the bonus pool structure creates a unique financial dynamic for the top finishers. Golf Digest Middle East listed the full payout for the top-10 in the season standings, starting with McIlroy’s $2 million reward. Eugenio Chacarra, who finished second in the race, received $1 million, while third-place finisher Hatton took $750,000. These figures come on top of the regular tournament checks earned at Jumeirah Golf Estates. The requirement to play at least four counting tournaments, including the finale, kept the field competitive until the very end. Yahoo reported that the top-10 players split a $6 million bonus pool, with the winner taking one-third of the total. This system rewards consistency over a full season, but it does not guarantee the biggest paycheck for the season champion if that player finishes outside the top spot in the final event. Who Actually Banked the Most Cash Tyrrell Hatton emerged as the biggest overall earner for the week, a fact that often gets lost in the celebration of McIlroy’s eighth title. GolfMagic reported that Hatton’s total earnings for the week reached $3.75 million after combining his tournament win with his season-long bonus. This sum includes his $3 million first-place prize and the $750,000 bonus for finishing third in the Race to Dubai standings. McIlroy’s total for the week came to $3.26 million, a massive sum that includes his $1.26 million tournament check and the $2 million season bonus. The difference between the two players highlights how the DP World Tour rewards both the season-long leader and the final tournament winner. Although Colin Montgomerie secured the former Order of Merit money title, Golf Digest Middle East verified that McIlroy has now joined him to share the record for most Race to Dubai titles in history. item.title: Pirates Add OF Chas McCormick on Minor-League Deal
item.description: The Pittsburgh Pirates have agreed to a minor-league deal with outfielder Chas McCormick, according to Ari Alexander of 7 News Boston. McCormick gets an invite to spring training. McCormick, a native of West Chester, Pa., totaled five big-league seasons with the Houston Astros from 2021-25 and won a World Series in 2022. His best season came in 2023, when he batted .273/.353/.489 with 17 doubles, two triples, 22 home runs, 70 RBI and 19 stolen bases in 115 games. Through his first three seasons with the Astros, McCormick compiled a robust .259/.336/.449 batting line with 41 doubles, four triples, 50 home runs, 164 RBI and 27 steals in 342 games. But from 2024-25, he batted just .211/.273/.301 with 11 doubles, one triple, six homers, 32 RBI and 10 steals in 158 games. The 31-year-old spent the 2026 season with Triple-A Iowa in the Chicago Cubs organization. He slashed .285/.383/.468 with 23 doubles, 14 home runs, 59 RBI and 17 steals in 102 games. McCormick has experience in all three outfield positions in his career. He’s totaled 245 games in left, 193 in center and 121 in right and has combined for a .995 fielding percentage and 13 defensive runs saved. The Astros originally drafted McCormick in the 21st round of the 2017 draft out of Millersville University of Pennsylvania. item.title: Match Awards from Germany’s magical 5-0 win over the Netherlands
item.description: (Photo by Odd ANDERSEN / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Germany are so back. In a troubling scenario heading into this match, Germany required all three points to have any chance of qualifying for the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals. In what was supposed to be a tightly contested match, Jürgen Klopp found some magic in his new squad scoring five against a Netherlands side that just came off a 7-0 thrashing of a solid Greek side. Jersey Swap: No one This one always feels harsh giving out but simply no one stood out from the pack in this Dutch side. What was actually a decent start for Xavi’s side in the first half was squandered by some missed scoring chances that really should have been put in the net. Thankfully for Germany, the Dutch were simply not clicking in this one. Der Kaiser: Nico Schlotterbeck While Nico Schlotterbeck might not have that illustrous aerial presence that Malick Thiaw offers, the Dortmund defender certainly showed off his heading with a brilliantly placed goal. Schlotterbeck was reliable defensively and offers much more going forward than other defenders. While Germany’s defense was never going to be the storyline of this match, it was ruthlessly efficient in thwarting anotherwise excellent Dutch attack, as shown in recent matches. Fussballgott: Joshua Kimmich The midfield was arguably the weakest side of the German team in this game and yet there was no bad performance to be found. Aleksander Pavlović and Kimmich were perhaps equally effective in this match and did a great job at picking up on the mistakes of a shaky Dutch performance. While many were disappointed to not see the recent duo of Tom Bischof and Pavlović share the midfield over this international break, it is clear that Kimmich and Pavlović are the main cast for the time being. Der Bomber: Florian Wirtz The Liverpool star did as he has done best in recent years, turning up for the German national team. While Wirtz was perhaps outshined by a certain winger by the end of the match, it was he who got things going for the Germans in the second half and created the momentum that they would ride for the rest of the match. The Ottawa Senators are off to a strong start in 2026-27, sitting 13-6-2 and in third place in a competitive Atlantic Division through 21 games. Not contributing much to that success is veteran winger Andre Burakovsky . The 31-year-old has gone pointless in eight games with Ottawa and hasn’t played since leaving a 6-5 overtime loss to the Los Angeles Kings with an injury Oct. 29. As Sportsnet hockey insider Elliotte Friedman reported on Saturday Headlines , the Senators are looking to move on from Burakovsky. Ottawa acquired him from the Chicago Blackhawks at the 2026 NHL Draft for a 2027 sixth-round pick. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Friedman added on Monday’s 32 Thoughts podcast that Ottawa could include Burakovsky in a larger trade. The Senators are looking to add to a core that has played well despite injuries to Jake Sanderson and William Eklund, among others. “I can’t say if this is going to be part of something to add, or it’s just going to be to move him and then create more opportunity to add,” Friedman said. Burakovsky has struggled since signing a five-year, $27.5 million contract with the Seattle Kraken ahead of the 2022-23 season. He helped the Colorado Avalanche win the Stanley Cup in 2022 before signing the deal. The winger put up 39 points in just 49 games in his first season with Seattle, but his production dipped from there. He managed 16 points in 49 games in 2023-24, 37 in 79 games in 2024-25 and 33 in 75 games with the Blackhawks last season. Now averaging just 11 minutes of ice time per game, Burakovsky has yet to carve out a role in Ottawa. His cap hit, declining production and lingering lower-body injury could make a standalone trade difficult. One league executive told the Ottawa Citizen’s Bruce Garrioch that Burakovsky is a “high-end talent,” while another said “he’s not that good a player.” The question now is whether the Austria-born forward plays another game for Ottawa as the Senators explore their options. item.description: USC’s Gabriel Ponce has his hand raised after beating Air Force’s Russell Klug to retain the WBC Collegiate title. LOS ANGELES — Gabriel “El Tigre” Ponce is still the WBC Collegiate champion. Ponce, a USC sophomore who fights out of St. Louis, Missouri, retained his title Saturday night with a unanimous decision over Air Force’s Russell Klug in the headliner of the Los Angeles Athletic Club’s Rivals in the Ring collegiate boxing invitational. The three-round, two-minutes-per-round fight was back-and-forth from the opening bell to the final one. Klug, a southpaw, applied forward pressure and tried to work from the center of the ring. Ponce countered that with timing and distance, going to the body to set up hooks to the head and slipping out of exchanges quickly before lining up his next attack. It was a sharp gameplan that won over the judges and the crowd. The card marked the first Rivals in the Ring at the LAAC since 2019, bringing live boxing back to the club whose boxing tradition dates to 1880. The bouts were held on the John R. item.description: LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 1: Declan Rice of Arsenal celebrates towards the fans following the Premier League 2026/27 match between Liverpool FC and Arsenal FC at Anfield on November 1, 2026 in Liverpool, United Kingdom. (Photo by Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images) | Getty Images Declan Rice will sign his new, five-year Arsenal contract soon, reports David Ornstein . The deal will keep him at the club through summer 2031, taking him past his 32nd birthday. Rice’s new contract follows on the heels of Jurrien Timber’s extension reported earlier today as well as Mikel Arteta putting pen to paper on an extension last month. For my money, Declan Rice is the best midfielder in the world. He does it all and that’s what makes him the best. There are other players in the world who can do specific things better but his combination of athleticism, game-reading, defensive application, attacking contribution, and set piece service is unique. If there was to be any criticism of his game coming into this season, it was his progressive passing. He generally fared better with an exceptional passer alongside him. In typical Declan Rice fashion, he’s patched that hole. He’s among the Premier League leaders in progressive passes and through balls this season and leads the competition with five assists. We can worry about Declan Rice’s ability and contribution levels towards the end of his new contract when we get there. You should always be a little leery of deals that take players beyond 30, particularly ones whose athleticism is a big part of what makes them great, but if any player is going to buck the age curve, it’s Declan Rice. The guy is a physical freak (in the best way). Given his high football I.Q., you’d also expect him to compensate for any decrease in speed, strength, whatever (if he experiences that at all) with veteran wiles. Arsenal are in win-now mode. item.title: PGA Tour Sponsorship Revenue Tops $1 Billion As Rival LIV Fades
item.description: PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp addresses a the media, tournament sponsors and Tour employees during a news conference on March 11 at the PGA Tour Global Home in Ponte Vedra Beach, Fla. The PGA Tour crossed a major financial milestone, as sponsorship revenue topped $1 billion for the first time. Mundo Deportivo reported the U.S.-based circuit saw a 14% increase in commercial income this year. This figure marks a new high for the organization after years of battling for control of professional golf. Strong partnerships with global brands drove this growth. Rolex renewed its multiyear deal to remain the official timekeeper across all tour platforms, according to Mundo Deportivo . Alongside Rolex, agreements with Amazon Web Services, Raymond James, and AbbVie added significant weight to the revenue total. The New Two-Tier Plan The tour is using this money to fund a major structural shift starting in 2028. The schedule will split into two distinct groups: the Championship Series and the Challenger Series. The top tier will feature about 130 players in 24 events, each with a minimum prize purse of $20 million. Players will have a defined route upward as the lower tier organizes 20 events featuring purses no less than $4 million. Dhruv Prasad, the PGA Tour’s chief commercial officer, stated the organization has secured deals for almost every future Championship Series tournament. Prasad believes the market response validates this direction. He mentioned that discussions are underway with multiple firms regarding partnerships for the Challenger Series. This structure aims to create more stability for sponsors and players alike. Old Deals Face Uncertainty Not every long-standing relationship is guaranteed to continue. FedEx, which has exclusively sponsored the FedEx Cup since 2007, has not confirmed whether its deal will continue beyond 2027. As the tour redirects its attention, the partnership remains under examination. The tour cannot rely solely on legacy sponsors to fund its future growth. Meanwhile, the rival LIV Golf circuit is fading fast. The Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund-backed group has begun shutting down after failing to relaunch its business. This collapse removes the primary threat that kept the PGA Tour on edge for five years. Strategic Sports Group has provided $1.5 billion in investment to the tour, funds that remain unspent. Those funds could improve facilities, hospitality, and ticketing operations. Long-Term Brand Power The extended partnership with Rolex underscores the enduring appeal of the sport’s history. The brand’s connection to golf predates the 2005 tour deal by nearly four decades. In 1967, the brand appointed Arnold Palmer, Jack Nicklaus, and Gary Player as its first golf Testimonees. Today, active stars like Scottie Scheffler, Brooks Koepka, and Justin Thomas carry that same status. The tour commands premium rates from advertisers.

item.title: Dowman's late winner as England Under-21s beat France
item.description: Under 21 Internationals England U21 3 - 2 France U21 FT Mikey Moore scored in Tottenham's EFL Cup win against Charlton earlier this season - and he got England's youngsters off to a flyer against France [Getty Images] Max Dowman's late strike gave England Under-21s a dramatic friendly win over France - after the Young Lions let a 2-0 lead slip away. The 16-year-old Arsenal prospect, making his first start for England at this level, tapped in to spare the blushes of hosts who had allowed their visitors to get back on terms late on. First-half goals from Mikey Moore and Divin Mubama gave European champions England a comfortable lead, a positive sign as they look for a third successive continental title in Serbia and Albania next year. But keeper Tommy Setford's own goal handed France a late lifeline, and Giovani Versini then equalised with five minutes left, before Dowman struck. The Young Lions will discover their Euro 2027 opponents on 26 November, with the draw held in Belgrade, yet boss Lee Carsley will not work with his squad again until March, leaving few chances to impress the head coach. After being frustrated in Friday's 1-0 defeat by Portugal, the hosts produced a composed and dominant display in Bristol as Moore scored his first England Under-21 goal after six minutes. The Tottenham forward has yet to score on loan at Cologne, who are fighting a relegation battle in the German Bundesliga, but here he calmly rolled past Mathieu Patouillet to cap a flowing move. Manchester City forward Mubama, on loan at Southampton this season, then added a second England goal after 29 minutes when he nodded in Ethan Nwaneri's deep cross. Nwaneri was twice denied in the second half as England chased a third goal, with Jovan Makama also testing Patouillet. England looked comfortable, but Setford's error, when he dropped Versini's looping effort, allowed France a way back. Versini's excellent 25-yard strike levelled the game, only for Dowman to have the final say when he scored from close range with a minute left.

item.description: Gleyber Torres is a free agent again, which leaves the Detroit Tigers without a second baseman for 2027. Detroit has to decide who fills that spot next season and for the years after it, and one of the names already attached to the Tigers is Luis Arraez .
